description: Savor the authentic taste of India with our Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, featuring succulent chicken marinated in a vibrant blend of yogurt and spices. Each piece is grilled to smoky perfection over charcoal, locking in a rich, tangy flavor and a beautifully charred exterior. This classic dish promises a delightful culinary journey right in your backyard.

instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them dry. Make deep gashes on the chicken pieces with a sharp knife to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply. Set aside.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp lemon juice, and salt. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another bowl, whisk together the yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and red food color (if using). Add 1 tbsp oil and mix well to form a smooth, thick marinade.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces to the second marinade, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create medium-high heat. The coals should be glowing red with a thin layer of ash.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill grate. Grill for 15-20 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and has beautiful char marks. Baste with remaining oil during the last 5-7 minutes of grilling to keep it moist and add flavor. Ensure internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the tandoori chicken from the grill. Garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings, or naan bread.

tips: For best results, marinate the chicken for at least 6-8 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to deeply penetrate the meat.
Ensure your charcoal grill reaches a medium-high heat before placing the chicken to achieve that perfect char without drying out the meat. Avoid overcrowding the grill.
Basting the chicken with oil or melted butter during the last few minutes of grilling will keep it moist, enhance the flavor, and add a beautiful sheen.
article:
Mastering the art of Indian cuisine at home can seem daunting, but some dishes are so iconic and satisfying that they’re worth the effort. Tandoori Chicken is undoubtedly one of them. While traditionally cooked in a scorching hot clay tandoor oven, recreating its magic on a charcoal grill brings an unparalleled smoky depth and char that makes for an unforgettable Indian dinner recipe. If you’re looking to impress your family and friends with a dish that’s bursting with flavor and aroma, then making your own **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** is an experience you won’t want to miss.

This article will guide you through everything you need to know to prepare succulent, perfectly grilled tandoori chicken, from the vibrant marinade to expert grilling techniques. Get ready to transform your backyard barbecue into an Indian feast!

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is a classic Indian dish originating from the Punjab region, famous for its vibrant red-orange color, tender meat, and distinctive smoky flavor. The name "tandoori" refers to the tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven used for cooking and baking in South Asia. In a tandoor, marinated chicken pieces are skewered and lowered into the intensely hot oven, cooking quickly and developing a beautiful char while remaining incredibly moist inside.

When we talk about **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**, we're essentially adapting this traditional method to a home setting using a charcoal grill. The charcoal imparts a similar smoky essence to the chicken, mimicking the tandoor's effect. The key to its flavor lies in the marinade: a rich blend of yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and a host of aromatic spices like cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili powder, and garam masala. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, breaking down the chicken fibers, while the spices infuse deep flavor into every bite. The result is a dish that's spicy, tangy, and incredibly flavorful, with that irresistible char from the grill.

## Ingredients You Need

To create authentic and delicious **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**, gather these essential ingredients:

For the Chicken:
*   2 lbs (approx. 1 kg) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs and drumsticks work best; breasts can be used but may dry out faster). You can also use a whole chicken cut into 8 pieces.
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice

For the First Marinade:
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   1 teaspoon salt
*   1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (or paprika for less heat)

For the Second Marinade:
*   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt works well for a thicker marinade)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tablespoon red chili powder (adjust to your spice preference)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1 tablespoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
*   1-2 drops red food coloring (optional, for that classic vibrant color)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any neutral oil like vegetable oil)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to prepare your amazing **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Pat the chicken pieces thoroughly dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits on each piece of chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply and helps the chicken cook evenly. Place the chicken in a large bowl.
2.  **First Marinade:** Drizzle the lemon juice over the chicken, then add 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder. Rub this mixture all over the chicken, ensuring it gets into the slits. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to an hour. This initial marinade helps tenderize the chicken and build a foundational flavor.
3.  **Second Marinade:** In a separate large bowl, combine all the ingredients for the second marinade: yogurt, 2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, ground coriander, ground cumin, garam masala, black pepper, salt, crushed kasuri methi (if using), red food coloring (if using), and mustard oil. Mix everything thoroughly until well combined.
4.  **Combine Marinades:** Add the chicken from the first marinade into the bowl with the second marinade. Make sure every piece of chicken is completely coated. Use your hands to really work the marinade into the slits and under the skin.
5.  **Marinate (The Longer, The Better):** Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, but ideally overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the chicken marinates, the more flavorful and tender it will be.
6.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to cook, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the coals for two-zone cooking (coals on one side, empty space on the other) for indirect heat, or spread them evenly for direct heat if you're comfortable managing flare-ups. Aim for a medium-high heat (around 375-400°F or 190-200°C). Clean and oil your grill grates to prevent sticking.
7.  **Grill the Chicken:** Remove the chicken from the refrigerator at least 30 minutes before grilling to bring it closer to room temperature. Skewer the chicken pieces if desired, or place them directly on the well-oiled grill grates. Start grilling over direct heat for 3-4 minutes per side to get a nice char, rotating frequently to prevent burning.
8.  **Finish Cooking:** Once charred, move the chicken to the cooler, indirect heat side of the grill. Close the lid and continue cooking for 20-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) at the thickest part. Flip the chicken every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking. The chicken should be cooked through, tender, and beautifully browned with charred spots.
9.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, keeping the chicken moist.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving perfect **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** requires a few expert tricks:

*   **Deep Slits are Key:** Don't be shy with the knife! Deeper slits mean more surface area for the marinade to penetrate, leading to more flavorful and tender chicken.
*   **Pat Dry for Better Char:** Excess moisture on the chicken skin will steam rather than sear. Patting the chicken thoroughly dry before marinating helps achieve that desirable crispy, charred exterior.
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt:** Use full-fat plain yogurt or Greek yogurt. The fat helps keep the chicken moist, and the thicker consistency of Greek yogurt helps the marinade cling better. Avoid low-fat or flavored yogurts.
*   **Long Marination:** This is perhaps the most crucial tip. While 4 hours is good, marinating overnight or even for 24 hours makes a significant difference in both flavor absorption and tenderness.
*   **Two-Zone Grilling:** This technique is a game-changer for charcoal grilling. Starting with direct heat for a quick char and then moving to indirect heat for slower cooking prevents burning the outside before the inside is done, especially for bone-in pieces.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook the chicken in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and leads to steaming instead of grilling, preventing a good char.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** The best way to ensure your chicken is cooked perfectly and safely is to use an instant-read meat thermometer. Chicken is done at 165°F (74°C).
*   **Basting (Optional):** Some like to brush the chicken with a little melted butter or ghee towards the end of cooking for extra richness and shine.

## Serving Suggestions

**Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** is a star dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, creating a complete Indian dinner:

*   **Naan or Roti:** Freshly baked naan bread or whole wheat roti are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its delicious juices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A simple bowl of fluffy basmati rice provides a neutral base that complements the rich flavors of the chicken.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip, often made with cucumber, mint, and spices, is an excellent counterpoint to the spicy chicken.
*   **Fresh Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice and cilantro) adds freshness and crunch.
*   **Chutneys:** Mint chutney, tamarind chutney, or even a spicy green chili chutney can elevate the experience.
*   **Lemon Wedges and Cilantro:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before serving brightens the flavors, and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro adds aroma and color.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic recipe is fantastic, there are ways to adapt your **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken** to suit different preferences or available ingredients:

*   **Chicken Cuts:** While bone-in pieces are traditional and tend to stay juicier, you can use boneless chicken thighs or breasts. Adjust grilling time accordingly; boneless pieces will cook faster.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For a milder version, use paprika. For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Cooking Method Alternatives:** If you don't have a charcoal grill, you can achieve a similar result using:
    *   **Gas Grill:** Preheat to medium-high heat. Follow the same direct/indirect cooking method. You won't get the same smoky flavor, but it will still be delicious.
    *   **Oven Broiler:** Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Broil for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until cooked through and charred.
    *   **Air Fryer:** Cook at 375°F (190°C) for 18-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until cooked and crispy.
*   **Vegetarian Version:** The tandoori marinade works beautifully with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), mushrooms, bell peppers, or cauliflower. Marinate and grill as you would the chicken.
*   **Smoky Flavor Enhancement:** If using a gas grill or oven, a little liquid smoke added to the marinade can provide a hint of that desired smoky taste.

Bringing the vibrant flavors of India to your home kitchen is a rewarding experience, and there's no better place to start than with a truly exceptional **Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken**. The deep marinade, combined with the unique char and smoky aroma from the grill, creates a dish that’s rich in history, flavor, and culinary satisfaction. So fire up your grill, embrace the spices, and get ready to enjoy one of the most beloved Indian dinner recipes right in your own backyard!
